summary: Gustav Hugo worked in history and archaeology and other fields. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1782–1785) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787–1788), and later held a post at Göttingen (~1788–1844).

Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Mensching studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Marburg, and under Rudolf Otto (~1922–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Roth worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, Munich, and Patna, he studied under Paul Thieme, Gaurinath Sastri, and others. He served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1855–1856), University of Leipzig (~1856–1858), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1858–1860), and Berlin University of the Arts, where he also held a post.
Linguist Guus Kroonen studied under doctoral supervisor Alexander Lubotsky (~2005–2009). He later held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Guy Claxton, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, founded the Sharpham College for Buddhist Studies and Contemporary Enquiry. He served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol's Graduate School of Education (attested 2006).

Stroumsa studied at Paris, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Harvard, and EPHE, and founded Hebrew University of Jerusalem. In religious studies, he held lecturer, associate professor, and editor roles at Hebrew University, and was later Emeritus Professor at Oxford (2009–2013).

Newland specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Virginia and studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and several Tibetan teachers. He served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Patrul Rinpoche.

Gyatsho Tshering worked in Tibetology after studying at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its Acting Director in 1972 and Director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda studied at Taisho University in the field of Buddhist studies. He later served as president (学長) of Taisho University (~1926–1944), professor (教授（嘱託）) at the University of Tokyo (1928), and lecturer (講師) at Toyo University.

Gyoei Takahashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Takahashi held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor (attested 2003–2004) and professor (attested 2026), and was a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (attested 2004).
Gyoin Hashimoto worked in Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1922–1925) and under Join Saeki. He served as head priest (管主) at Yakushi-ji from 1939 to 1967.

Gyoko Iotani studied at Rissho University (~1968–1978) in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University as assistant professor, professor, and emeritus professor (~1983–~2020), and was formerly a specially appointed professor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyokusen Hosaka studied at Komazawa University in the field of Buddhist studies. He later served as president (学長) of Komazawa Junior College.
Gyomay Kubose was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Otani University (~1936–1941) and was a student of Haya Akegarasu.
Gyoon Iotani works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a post as deputy director (副主任) at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Gyosho Takahashi worked in Buddhist studies. He held a post as professor (教授) at Minobusan University, attested in 1992 and 1996.
Gyoshu Nakajo worked in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor (教授) at Minobusan University (attested 1996), where he was also a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934). He later held a post at Nyugat.
